title: Fortescue Zero to compete in Formula E with Racing and Innovation Team
excerpt:
Making history as the first Australian owned outfit to race in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship, Fortescue Zero will join the grid from the start of the upcoming 2026/27 season - subject to FEO and FIA approval.

This is far from Fortescue’s first foray into motorsport, from its roots in Williams Racing (as Williams Advanced Engineering), to becoming an in-demand, high-performance engineering business, working at the cutting edge of electrification as the Official PIT BOOST supplier of Formula E.

To set the groundwork for this exciting new chapter, Fortescue has acquired the Penske Formula E operation and will compete with a Jaguar GEN4 powertrain.

Capable of reaching speeds in excess of 335kph, 0-100kph in approximately 1.8 seconds, and 0-200kph in just 4.4 seconds - 1.5 seconds faster than its predecessor - GEN4 will deliver 50% more power in race mode than the current GEN3 Evo race car. The GEN4 car will be an average of 10 seconds faster per lap than the GEN3 car in qualifying mode. In ATTACK MODE, GEN4 produces up to 600kW of power, a 71% increase in base output over GEN3 Evo, delivering performance that pushes the limits of electric racing. GEN4 is the only single-seater race car with permanent all-wheel drive.

Gus Pichot, Fortescue Growth and Energy CEO, said: “For more than a decade Fortescue Zero has been the brains behind some of the groundbreaking technologies powering and transforming electric racing. Now, we’re going to show the world how we can compete on the track as well.

“Progressing from the pit lane to the grid is the next chapter in our motorsports story. We’re here to race, to win and to innovate.

“At Fortescue it’s in our DNA to go to the extreme, push the limits and go further and faster than our competitors. For us, motorsports is more than just a chance to take home a championship trophy, it’s a platform to develop, test and hone in on the next great technologies that will transform industries beyond racing.”

Jeff Dodds, Formula E CEO, said: “Fortescue Zero has been a vital technology partner for Formula E from day one, standing alongside us since the inception of the Championship.”

“Formula E is far more than a racing series, it’s an incubator for peak performance and ground-breaking technology, and Fortescue Zero exemplifies both.”

“We are excited to see the competitive edge and innovation they will bring to the GEN4 era of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.”

title: “A sense of duty done”: Lucas di Grassi’s final Formula E chapter
excerpt:
For over a decade, Lucas di Grassi has played a critical role in Formula E’s history.

From taking victory in the championship’s inaugural race at the 2014 Beijing E-Prix, to his final race in London, the Brazilian has been in Formula E for every chapter: the victories, championship battles, all the highs and lows, ultimately ending at the conclusion of the 2025/26 season, as the 42-year-old makes the decision to retire from professional racing.

Di Grassi is a figure that most knowledgeable motorsport fans will be familiar with, having competed in Formula One, The World Endurance Championship (WEC), and GT World Cup. But Formula E has undoubtedly been the championship where he has spent the longest part of his 24-year career.

His involvement in the series goes even further back than the first time the original GEN1 cars hit the track, with the Brazilian playing a critical role in the development of the foundation of the championship and its early prototype machinery.

READ MORE: The history of Formula E's race cars: GEN1-2-3 to GEN3 Evo and GEN4

As he looks back on his career, however, he says it’s difficult to decide how he will be remembered: “​The memories are not what I choose them to be. It's the experiences I had with people that I interacted with, and people watching the races, people that I worked with, so it's very hard to choose what the others will remember.

“I was pushing people very, very hard. I had fights all the time. I had good moments, but also bad moments. I would say in racing, I had way more bad moments and good moments.

“​The amount of hours, the amount of time away from home, the number of times in crappy hotels and missing birthdays, like this year where my son had his birthday during the Shanghai E-Prix, actually, so it was a cool birthday present (claiming victory). But I still missed a lot of birthdays, weddings, friend celebrations, and so on.

“I made a lot of commitments. I put in a lot of effort. I can say that I'm the driver who put the most effort into Formula E, and I hope people see it this way because it's not only the drivers or the people working for me, but it’s everybody who created the memories.”

The early seasons

As the winner of the first-ever Formula E E-Prix, di Grassi didn’t have to wait very long for his first victory in the all-electric championship.

The first year of Formula E was a season like no other - the first of its kind - with the grid having names like Nico Prost, Nelson Piquet Jr, and Bruno Senna, but with many motorsport fans and journalists still getting used to the concept of electric racing.

Nicolas Prost took pole for the first-ever E-Prix, and looked set to claim Formula E’s first silverware, but a dramatic final lap changed the result and gave the championship one of its most famous moments...

German Nick Heidfeld attempted to overtake Prost for the lead of the race into the final corner, with the resulting collision sending Heidfeld into the air, and ultimately the barrier. Thankfully, both drivers escaped unharmed, but their retirements allowed di Grassi, who had spent much of the race in third, to take the lead and cross the line as the first-ever Formula E winner. It was the first of his 13 victories.

WATCH: Huge crash in Formula E's first-ever race! - Prost vs Heidfeld incident

Another one of his most notable wins came three seasons later in Mexico City, where he started the E-Prix from 15th on the grid, with his race appearing to be over after a first-lap collision damaged his rear wing and forced him to pit for repairs. However, a Safety Car on Lap 18 gave Audi the opportunity to call di Grassi in for his mandatory pit stop and switch to his second car. The strategy meant he would have to make his second battery last for 28 laps.

When the race leader eventually pitted, di Grassi miraculously took control of the race, running an extreme energy-saving mode strategy while defending from Jean-Eric Vergne. Despite the challenge facing him, di Grassi held on to the lead and took victory.

Later that year, di Grassi then finished seventh in the Montreal finale, which was enough to secure the 2016/17 Drivers' Championship, despite Sebastien Buemi holding a 10-point advantage over the Brazilian driver heading into the final race. Unfortunately for Buemi, a 10-place grid penalty, due to a practice crash and battery replacement put the Swiss driver on the backfoot and helped neutralise his advantage.

Looking back at the publicised rivalry between the two Formula E Titans at the time, he said: “At the time, I hated him. When you are competing, you want to win. Of course, you have to have that spirit, and if you don't have that spirit, you should not be a professional sportsman.

“He was the guy to beat. I had him in my mind, many, many days of my life, that I was on the treadmill, and I put myself to run 10 kilometers. At the end of the 10km, I would say, no, no, no, I need to beat him, I'm gonna run another two. And that pushes you outside of your comfort zone, which makes you go to areas that you never go to in a normal day life. I said to him (Buemi), thank you very much for pushing me.

WATCH: "You are my champion" - Formula E says goodbye to Lucas di Grassi

“Now, I look back and I'm very thankful for that rivalry and the fact that we had that competition. I only achieved what I achieved because I had to pull myself out of my comfort zone.”

The start of a lifelong passion

Di Grassi’s path to the top step of motorsport was anything but straightforward. With no family background in competitive racing, he began his career at his uncle’s kart shop in Interlagos, making his competitive karting debut at the age of 10. From there, he progressed through the junior-single seater ranks, winning the Macau Grand Prix in 2005 and finishing runner-up in the GP2 series (the predecessor of FIA Formula 2) before reaching Formula One with Virgin in 2010. In 2012, he became an Audi factory driver, giving his career a degree of stability after years of moving between different categories.

When asked if there was anything he would’ve done differently, he said: “The only thing I learned through my career that I wish I'd learned earlier is to focus on what I want and only on what I can control. I would tell my younger self to keep doing what I'm doing, worry a bit less, and focus on the process instead of trying to imagine the future.

“There were a lot of ifs, and if I look at the negatives, there was a chance I would never make it out of karting. I wouldn't have even started karting if my father hadn't asked me to go and try it.

“If I didn't want to race for Alejandro (Agag) in Formula 2, I probably wouldn't have been involved in Formula E. That relationship created a long-term connection, when I started the series, he was the first one involved.

“​I have zero regrets. I think that if you gave 100% of what you could do in that specific moment, and you thought it through as best as you could, that's a decision.”

One decision, however, would have a lasting impact on the latter stages of his career. After Audi vacated its Formula E license at the end of 2021, di Grassi joined Venturi for what was ultimately a one-season spell. He made an immediate impression, taking victory at the 2022 London E-Prix, Round 14. It was the result that appeared to put him in an ideal position to continue with the team as it transitioned into the GEN3 era under the Maserati name.

Instead, di Grassi chose to join Mahindra Racing, a decision he now describes as his biggest career mistake. He explained, “One decision, for example, was that I could have stayed at Maserati, but I signed with Mahindra. By the time I went to Mahindra, Dilbagh (Gill) left Mahindra. So the guy that signed me, and I went there; there was no CEO anymore.

“I had Mahindra, then I had the CUPRA, which used the Mahindra powertrain, which wasn't great at the time. Then I started a new project with Lola, and it was like starting from scratch again.”

He continued, “What you have to understand is that in the life of a racing driver, most of the time, you don't know what you're going to do next year. So you finish the season, and you don't even have the money, or you don't have the team, or nothing. You're fighting for your life every year. It's very stressful. That's life. I don't regret it.”

READ MORE: Lucas di Grassi announces retirement from Formula E

Saying goodbye to Formula E

Di Grassi closed his Formula E chapter at the London ExCeL, hanging up his racing suit with a smile, after a bittersweet weekend.

Carrying a three place-grid penalty from the penultimate double-header of the season in Tokyo for failing to slow down under Red Flags, di Grassi started Saturday’s race from the back of the grid. His afternoon then unravelled further. A five-second penalty for speeding under a Full Course Yellow was followed by a technical failure on Lap 19 that sent him into the barriers and brought his race into an early end.

Sunday’s race offered little consolation. The Lola Yamaha ABT driver was forced to stop during Free Practice 3 with another technical problem, before being handed a 20-place grid penalty, which was converted into a 10-second stop-and-go penalty. Once again, luck decided to not be on his side. After 18 laps, his engineer instructed him to stop the car due to an electrical issue, bringing his final Formula E race to an abrupt conclusion.

Yet, despite the disappointment in the season finale, di Grassi had already written a fitting final chapter just a few weeks earlier. His unexpected victory in Shanghai gave him one last taste of success and one last visit to the Formula E podium.

REPORT: Di Grassi seals spectacular Shanghai E-Prix Round 13 win on final lap

As he left the paddock on Sunday evening, di Grassi was able to look back on his career with a sense of satisfaction. He asserted, “It was an amazing run. Unfortunately, I exploded 3 power trains, so there was nothing I could do, but you wouldn't have changed much.

“I think we took the victory in Shanghai as the high point of the season. I retire with a sense of duty done.

“I'm sad, but I'm happy that it's over. I'm relieved. I have a lot of plans in my head that I wanted to accomplish for many years now. I'm gonna focus on those, but I will keep coming to Formula E.”

title: Paysafe Envision confirm Zak O'Sullivan for 2026/27 Formula E season
excerpt:
Paysafe Envision Formula E Team today has announced that Zak O’Sullivan will join the team as a full-time driver, stepping up after a year of development work within the team; including simulator duties, as well as driving in several rookie tests.

O’Sullivan’s first run with the team came ahead of the Season 11 Jeddah E-Prix, where he made his Formula E debut during the Rookie Free Practice session.

“I am very excited to be joining the team full-time for the upcoming season," says O'Sullivan. "I’ve spent the last year embedding myself into the team and can’t wait to get the season started in the new GEN4 car.

"Formula E is a championship I’ve had my sights set on for a long time, so to be joining the grid for Season 13 at such an exciting time for the sport is a great feeling.”

Since his first test with the team, O’Sullivan has driven the GEN3 Evo on a further three occasions during Season 12, in Berlin, Miami and Madrid– with the 21-year-old topping he timesheets during the Miami E-Prix rookie session.

O’Sullivan arrives with an impressive racing CV. After numerous wins in karting, the British driver moved into single-seater racing and narrowly missed out on the 2020 British Formula 4 title before winning the GB3 Championship the following year.

Two seasons in FIA Formula 3 followed, including four victories and the championship runner-up spot in 2023, before he stepped up to FIA Formula 2 in 2024 and claimed standout wins in Monaco and Spa-Francorchamps.

O’Sullivan has since broadened his experience in Japanese Super Formula, adding further depth to a career that has already demonstrated speed, adaptability and racewinning pedigree across multiple categories.

“We are very happy to announce Zak as a full-time driver for Season 13 and beyond," says Sylvain Filippi, Managing Director & CTO, Paysafe Envision Formula E Team.

"We’ve spent a lot of time with him during Season 12, and he has established himself in the team very well.

"We have been very impressed with Zak’s performance, both on the track during the rookie sessions, and his commitment off-track.

"We are very much looking forward to seeing him race in our car and embarking on his rookie season in Formula E with us.”

Franz Jung, Vice President of Envision Energy and CEO & Chairman of the Board of Paysafe Envision Formula E Team adds: “It is great to confirm our driver line-up for Season 13, with Zak joining us for his rookie season in the sport.

"Investing in young talent for the new generation of the sport was very important to us, and we are excited to see Zak step up into his new role as full-time driver.

"With our driver-line up complete, title sponsorship confirmed and an incredibly exciting new era of the sport ahead of us, we are very much looking forward to round one.”

title: Max Günther joins Paysafe Envision Racing
excerpt:
Following his exit from DS PENSKE, Maximilian Günther has moved to Paysafe Envision Formula E Team for the 2026/27 Formula E season.

It’s a new era for the Paysafe Envision Formula E Team, as the British-based squad welcomes a new Title Partner and a completely new driver line-up for the 2026/27 season - the first of the GEN4 era.

As such, the team have called on the services of former DS PENSKE driver, and Formula E race winner, Maximilian Günther, who has signed a multi-year contract to bring his wealth of experience to the Paysafe Envision squad.

During his eight seasons in the championship, Günther has been no stranger to the top step of the podium, winning seven E-Prix’s, the first of which made him Formula E’s youngest-ever race winner - a record only recently beaten by Taylor Barnard.

However, the 2025/26 season was a challenging one for the young German driver, who finished 18th in the Drivers’ standings with 23 points and a best finish of sixth. He will no doubt, therefore be looking forward to a fresh start with the Paysafe Envision squad, behind-the-wheel of the GEN4 - Formula E’s fastest car to date.

Capable of reaching speeds in excess of 335kph, 0-100kph in approximately 1.8 seconds, and 0-200kph in just 4.4 seconds - 1.5 seconds faster than its predecessor - GEN4 will deliver 50% more power in race mode than the current GEN3 Evo race car. The GEN4 car will be an average of 10 seconds faster per lap than the GEN3 car in qualifying mode. In ATTACK MODE, GEN4 produces up to 600kW of power, a 71% increase in base output over GEN3 Evo, delivering performance that pushes the limits of electric racing. GEN4 is the only single-seater race car with permanent all-wheel drive.

Maximillian Günther, Paysafe Envision Formula E Team driver, said: “I’m very happy to become a Paysafe Envision Formula E driver for the GEN4 era and I really look forward to our future together.

“The team has a very successful history in Formula E and exceptional quality throughout the organisation. Our aim is to combine our strengths and achieve great success, competing at the very top. I truly believe we have all the ingredients to build something really special together.

“What convinced me about the project was the great environment, the high ambition of the team, the mindset and, of course, the excellent technical package together with Jaguar.

I’m proud to become part of the team and have a fantastic feeling about our future.”

Sylvain Filippi, Managing Director & CTO of Paysafe Envision Formula E Team, said: “We are thrilled to announce Max as our newest driver at Paysafe Envision Formula E Team. Season 13 is going to be an important year for all teams; learning the GEN4 car as well as a new sporting format, which is going to put an even bigger focus on outright pace and speed.

“Max has proven how capable he is at delivering qualifying laps when it matters, as well as podium finishes and race wins. We’re incredibly excited to start working with him and hit the ground running at pre-season testing in November.”

title: Lessons, podium finishes, and what comes next for Pepe Martí
excerpt:
Pepe Martí’s debut campaign in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship established the 21-year-old CUPRA KIRO driver as 'one to watch' in the paddock!

Pepe Martí had a rookie season he could scarcely have imagined when he joined Formula E paddock at the start of the 2025/26 season. Not only did the CUPRA KIRO driver achieve two podium finishes and end the year as the highest placed rookie, but he also made history as the first Spaniard in the championship to secure a podium.

The CUPRA KIRO driver took home 66 championship points, enough to beat fellow rookie Felipe Drugovich by just one point. However, Marti narrowly missed out on a place inside the top-10, with Round 16 (the first of the London double-header finale weekend) resulting in disappointment and a point less finish. Tokyo was also a weekend of mixed emotions, with a DNF in the second race of the weekend - the day after his teammate Dan Ticktum snatched a dramatic victory from Andretti’s Jake Dennis.

“The race (Round 16 in London) ended up with a DNF, which is what you never want," said Martí. "We got quite unlucky with the Full Course Yellow. It was thrown out for about one lap so about seven cars got a really good advantage. We weren't in that group, unfortunately. We had a good pace. I was moving forward. I would have probably finished right in front of Oliver (Rowland) in P10, so we could have scraped a point, but we weren't able to. I was not happy with myself.”

“Ideally we want to finish on a good result and on the high notes as well. Most of the team is English, it's a home race for most of them. So it would’ve also been nice for them to be able to score a good result. If I'm honest today, the main limiting factor was qualifying.”

Marti responded in the following round - the final race of the 2025/26 championship campaign - taking eighth after starting from 13th on the grid (he was classified 11th in qualifying but started 13th due to a grid penalty).

Marti maintained 13th for most of the title-deciding race before completing his two ATTACK MODE activations on Lap 23 and 31. He then battled his way into the top-10 over the final four laps to take home eighth, making it a total of 128 points for CUPRA KIRO, securing the squad its most successful campaign in Formula E to date.

“I wasn’t really happy, but I guess that goes for everyone, right? Everyone apart from the winner isn't happy,” he continued. “It's not the greatest weekend of my life, but at least we got something out of it. I managed to help with people who I needed to help during the race and also finish my own race in a good position and obviously take away some points which I'm quite grateful for in this situation than I was in five races ago.

NEWS: Pepe Martí continues with CUPRA KIRO for 2026/27 season

“I have no regrets. Obviously, there are a lot of things that I would like to improve this season and I wouldn't really call it a regret. It's stuff that I want to get better at, stuff that I need to improve and obviously stuff that as a team we need to understand and move forward.”

Marti’s racecraft and determined approach to recovering from setbacks were the highlights of his debut campaign, as he managed to score nine points finishes from 17 races and proved many critics wrong. Now, however, the 21-year-old driver is ready to leave his rookie season behind and turn his attention to a new chapter for the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship - GEN4.

“We need to regroup, and come back a bit stronger next year," he asserts. “I need some time off as a whole, since 2025 even in Formula 2, I haven't had some time off and I need to sort of really, really disconnect from the motorsport world. I just want to be alone with my family, have some time off, enjoy the time with friends, the good weather, the good food, and a lot of cycling, get back in shape. In the championship, it's very hard to maintain proper shape so we can try to get better in the winter and come back stronger in December.”

Pepe Martí will continue with CUPRA KIRO for the 2025/27 Formula E season.

title: Pepe Martí continues with CUPRA KIRO for 2026/27 season
excerpt:
After a podium winning rookie season, Pepe Martí is set to continue with the CUPRA KIRO squad into Formula E's all-new GEN4 era.

Martí, who hails from Spain and is managed by A14, the driver development group co-founded by former Formula 1 World Champion Fernando Alonso, impressed many in the paddock with his on track performances in the 2025/26 season.

After scoring points in only his second E-Prix appearance, and leading his home race in Madrid, he achieved his maiden Formula E podium in Monaco - putting on a brilliant performance, after starting from 15th. Not only was the podium a significant milestone for Martí, but it also marked the first time a Spanish driver had reached the rostrum in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

READ MORE: Pepe Martí makes his mark in Monaco

A further podium (a second place) followed at the 2026 Sanya E-Prix, with the additional points helping the CUPRA KIRO driver to finish the season as the highest-placed rookie in the Drivers’ Championship with 66 points.

Continuing with CUPRA KIRO, Martí will play a crucial role in the team’s next chapter as Formula E enters the GEN4 era, the most exciting chapter to date in the all-electric championship.

Capable of reaching speeds in excess of 335kph, 0-100kph in approximately 1.8 seconds, and 0-200kph in just 4.4 seconds - 1.5 seconds faster than its predecessor - GEN4 will deliver 50% more power in race mode than the current GEN3 Evo race car. The GEN4 car will be an average of 10 seconds faster per lap than the GEN3 car in qualifying mode. In ATTACK MODE, GEN4 produces up to 600kW of power, a 71% increase in base output over GEN3 Evo, delivering performance that pushes the limits of electric racing. GEN4 is the only single-seater race car with permanent all-wheel drive.

Unleashing GEN4: A new era of high-performance, sustainable electric racing begins

Pepe Martí, CUPRA KIRO Driver, said: “I’m very excited to continue with CUPRA KIRO for the 2026/27 Formula E season. I’ve felt a huge amount of support and trust since joining the team, and together, I think we’ve built something really positive during my rookie year. Formula E has been an incredible learning experience, and I feel that I’ve grown a lot as a driver over the course of the season. To have achieved top three finishes, led races, and become the first Spanish driver to stand on the Formula E podium is something I’m very proud of, but I also feel like we’re only just getting started. CUPRA KIRO has big ambitions for the future, and I’m excited to be part of the journey for GEN4. I can’t wait to see what we can achieve next season.”

Russell O’Hagan, CUPRA KIRO Team Principal, said: “Continuing our relationship with Pepe for the 2026/27 season was a very straightforward decision. Since the moment he joined the team, he has consistently impressed us with his talent, work ethic, and maturity. As a championship, Formula E can be particularly demanding for rookie drivers, especially at the end of a generation cycle, so our priority was always to allow Pepe the time and environment to develop without unnecessary pressure.

"The reality is, however, that he exceeded our expectations almost immediately and showed consistent performance across season. Watching Pepe grow over the course of the season was incredibly rewarding. He’s developed his understanding of Formula E’s nuances at an impressive rate, grown in confidence with every race, and delivered performances that have demonstrated exactly why we believed in him in the first place. We firmly believe he’s one of the sport’s brightest young talents and ambassadors, and that he has all the attributes to become a major force in Formula E. We’re incredibly proud of everything that Pepe has achieved during his rookie season, and the team’s role in getting him up to speed – it was a big group effort. We’re equally excited that he’ll continue his journey with CUPRA KIRO as we enter GEN4. We’re only at the beginning of what we believe we can achieve together.”

title: Zane Maloney joins Oliver Rowland at Nissan for 2026/27
excerpt:
Nissan have announced Zane Maloney will join the team alongside Oliver Rowland for the 2026/27 ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

Rowland continues into a fourth year, having built a strong relationship with the Japanese manufacturer over the years, having originally joined its Formula E program as a rookie in Season 5 (2018/19) - Nissan's first year in the sport.

Since returning to the team during the GEN3 era in Season 10 (2023/24), Rowland has enjoyed some of the most successful years of his career, including claiming the Drivers' title in Season 11. In the last campaign, he earned six podiums, including a victory on the streets of Monaco, securing fourth in the Drivers' World Championship and maintaining his record of top-four finishes in every season since his return.

"I'm delighted to continue with Nissan for our seventh season together and fourth consecutive one with Nissan," says the 34-year-old. "With the GEN4 car coming in, we're going to see a big step in performance and it's something we're really excited for.

"I'm looking forward to Zane joining the team, he's had a great junior career and two years of experience in Formula E, which puts him in a good position to start Season 13 strongly. Heading into the future with Nissan Formula E Team is very exciting and we're aiming to improve on our performances from this year."

Maloney joins Nissan

Meanwhile, Maloney enters his third season in Formula E, having gained valuable experience across his first two campaigns, scoring top-10 finishes in São Paulo, Monaco and Tokyo in 2025/26.

The Barbadian earned his opportunity in Formula E after a highly successful junior career, impressing across the 2023 and 2024 Formula 2 seasons with 11 podiums, including two wins, and finishing fourth in the last year. His Formula E experience, combined with his proven pace in Formula 2, will provide a strong foundation as he enters the GEN4 era with Nissan.

"I'm very excited to join Nissan," says the 22-year-old. "When I came into Formula E, the team was winning the championship with Oli, so it's a great chance for me to now join a top manufacturer.

"I've spent the last two seasons with a new team, developing my skills and trying to get the best results we could, so I'm really looking forward to taking this next step in my career.

"It's also a great opportunity to be teammates with Oli. He's a World Champion and someone I watched when I was growing up, first winning races in Formula 2 and then in Formula E, so to be alongside him and learn from him will be really valuable.

"GEN4 is a big opportunity for everyone to develop quickly, and I'll be doing everything I can to prepare well and hit the ground running from the first race. A big thank you to Nissan for the trust in me. I'm really looking forward to getting started and achieving some very good results together."

title: Opel finalises 2026/27 line-up with Mitch Evans signing
excerpt:
Opel GSE has confirmed the capture of one of the most successful drivers in ABB FIA Formula E World Championship history with Mitch Evans joining the squad from the 2026/27 season.

The 32-year-old New Zealander has achieved the most victories in the racing series - 16 - and brings his experience from 10 years in the series to the new German manufacturer team.

Together with rookie Théo Pourchaire, Evans forms what Opel GSE view as a driver mix of top driver and young talent, underpinning the team's ambitions to compete at the front field from the start.

Dream team: Mitch Evans 'the preferred candidate from the beginning'

“We have secured our dream team. Mitch Evans was the preferred candidate for our Opel GSE Formula E Team from the very beginning. His commitment once again underlines the seriousness of the entire project,” said Opel Motorsport Director and Team Principal Jörg Schrott.

“We have already met Mitch on and off the racetrack. In addition to his undisputed exceptional sporting pedigree, he also fits perfectly into our team as a person. After so many years with another manufacturer, he was deliberately looking for a new challenge.

"Now the Opel family and Mitch are taking this next step together. In doing so, we are sending a clear message: We are joining the World Championship to challenge at the front.”

Evans: 'Perfect moment for a fresh challenge'

Evans himself is looking forward to the change and the cooperation with Opel. “I am proud to be an Opel works driver and to be part of this new chapter in Formula E. It’s great that we can finally make this step official,” said Evans.

“After ten years with a manufacturer, it was time for me to take on a fresh challenge. The leap to the GEN4 cars represents the perfect moment to start something new. I immediately felt how much energy and passion Opel is putting into the Formula E project.

"The team isn’t just coming into the series to compete: Opel is here to win, and that’s exactly what I aspire to.”

After a dramatic final weekend in London, Evans was narrowly denied the first Drivers' World Championship title of his career, but once again underlined his position among Formula E's best.

“The title clearly remains the big goal for me, in this respect I still have a score to settle in Formula E. That’s exactly why the move to Opel feels like the right new challenge for me.

"Starting a new Formula E generation with a new team and being successful right away is anything but a matter of course, but that’s exactly what appeals to me. I want to contribute my experience from ten years of Formula E and play a strong role in the World Championship together with Opel and Théo.”

Opel: 'Formula E the perfect stage for high-performance Mokka GSE and Corsa GSE'

Evans made his first official appearance in Opel colours this week as a surprise guest at the international media drive of the new battery-electric Opel Corsa GSE2.

This is just one example of how closely Opel is set to tie its production models with its halo motorsport project; using Formula E as a stage for its all-electric high-performance models.

After the Mokka GSE, which is already on the roads, the Corsa GSE will be launched this year and will make its trade fair debut at the Paris Motor Show in October.

The completion of the driver line-up, which includes Test and Development Driver Sophia Flörsch in addition to Evans and Pourchaire, marks Opel’s next step on the way to the World Championship.

Confirmation of its line up follows the Rüsselsheim-based manufacturer's commitment to the Opel GSE Formula E Team and the world premiere of the Opel GSE 27FE prototype at Le Castellet.

The next major milestone is coming this autumn, when Opel, together with Evans and Pourchaire, will unveil the final design of the race car for the 2026/27 season at the Paris Motor Show on 12 October 2026.

title: Buemi seals 2025/26 ABB Engineered to Outrun Award, while Mortara and Nato end on a high
excerpt:
As the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship reached a dramatic conclusion in London, the finale also heralded two new ABB Engineered to Outrun Award winners – and the overall triumph for a championship legend.

Edoardo Mortara and Norman Nato secured the honours as the biggest risers across the two races in the English capital, marking their first Engineered to Outrun success of the season.

Though the tense title fight naturally stole headlines, Mortara and Nato scoring points from unlikely starting positions on Saturday and Sunday respectively showed the kind of class that runs deep through the field – even if it is out of the immediate spotlight.

Mortara started down in 18th for Saturday’s PIT BOOST race. He ran a longer first stint before his mandatory charging stop, saving a small but critical 2% extra energy compared to the median in the field in the process.

This allowed him to unleash more pace when others diving into the pits gave him clear air, aided by Mortara using six minutes of ATTACK MODE deployment. Though there was a full-course yellow to nullify the last minute and a half of this power advantage, it also facilitated a cheaper pitstop.

That perfect combination meant Mortara leapt from 15th to 8th around the pitstop phase, and the energy advantage he retained after the pitstop allowed him to not only consolidate his position but push on even further.

He was actually fifth at the chequered flag but a final move on Dan Ticktum proved slightly too robust, so a small time penalty relegated him to seventh.

Still, it was a very effective performance – and the manner of his drive turned out to be neatly prescient for what followed a day later, when Mortara completed a Mahindra one-two in qualifying and finished Sunday's race on the podium.

Nato ends on a high

When the season finale exploded into life in the final few laps, claiming various point-scoring casualties in and around the top 10, it presented a clear opportunity for anyone who could keep it clean and be poised to pounce.

Nato was one such driver. Having started towards the back of the field, Nato made little progress from his 19th place grid position for much of the race, as he focused on an extreme energy-saving tactic - building a surplus of more than 5% versus the grid’s median.

By the time he opted to engage ATTACK MODE in the final third of the E-Prix he had moved just one position forward. But that ATTACK MODE timing was absolutely perfect to capitalise on the drama that engulfed the championship battle and massively impacted the lower reaches of the top 10.

Nato gained eight of his nine positions in that phase of the race, and was already on the move in the midfield when a multi-car collision vaulted him to 11th. The last seconds of his ATTACK MODE helped move him into ninth and though team-mate Oliver Rowland's late double ATTACK MODE burst meant the Nissans swapped positions again, this race still ended with Nato snatching a very unlikely point.

Though this has not been a grand season to remember for the championship returnee, he at least ensured it ended on a relative high with just his fourth points finish of the year.

Buemi wins overall

But it was Sebastien Buemi, together with race engineer Connor Summerville, who topped the final leaderboard for the season – pipping Lucas di Grassi and Markus Michelberger by just two places having gained 89 positions over the 17 races this year.

As Buemi leaves Envision Racing after this season, his Formula E future is unknown. The 2015/16 champion has been one of the grid’s most impressive stalwarts with 14 wins, 36 podiums and 1,172 points scored and that experience and class has been at the centre of a strong season.

Buemi has been in the points 11 times out of 17, exemplified by two final flourishes in London where he turned 10th place on the grid in both races to fourth and fifth at the finish.

title: Porsche's GEN3 racer to debut in Need for Speed Mobile
excerpt:
Following its recent launch into one of China's largest mobile games, Game for Peace, the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship has teamed up with Tencent once again.

Starting 21 August, players in China will be able to take the wheel of the title-winning Porsche GEN3 99X Electric, bringing peak electric performance, high-torque acceleration, and energy recovery mechanics to Need for Speed Mobile.

Porsche GEN3 99X Electric in the Hall of Legends

Positioned in the prestigious 'Hall of Legends - Hybrid & Electric Drive' vehicle class, the Porsche GEN3 99X Electric introduces a distinct driving profile specifically calibrated to tackle the high-speed streets of Need for Speed Mobile.

Engineered to replicate the real-world dynamics of Porsche's official Formula E factory contender, the in-game machine boasts several unique handling traits:

Agile Drift Tuning: Features more agile rear-tail behavior during drifts, allowing drivers to carry higher entry speeds through tight corners and execute sharper turn-ins.

High Torque Endurance: Delivers a significantly higher base top speed, precision steering response, and automatic nitrous accumulation while cornering.

ERS Regenerative Braking System: Replicating the 99X Electric’s real-world powertrain management, the Energy Recovery System (ERS) delivers a sustained high-torque launch boost for 2.8 seconds from a standstill. During braking, handbrake turns, and inertia drifts, the system harvests kinetic energy - temporarily lowering top speed - before unleashing the stored power within 2 seconds post-drift for a massive nitrous boost

Exclusive 'Hot Pursuit Mode' capabilities

Beyond standard sprint and circuit battles, driving the Porsche GEN3 99X Electric unlocks dedicated operational perks within Need for Speed Mobile’s high-stakes Hot Pursuit game mode - the classic gameplay format that features intense chases between Street Racers and Pursuit Teams:

Street Racer Role: Equipping the Porsche 99X Electric expands overall backpack capacity, giving racers the room needed to carry extra tactical supplies during intense escapes.

Pursuit Team Role: Drivers taking on the enforcement role will completely eliminate the helicopter cooldown timer while operating the vehicle, maintaining continuous aerial surveillance over targets.

How to unlock: 'Hall Treasures' event

The Porsche GEN3 99X Electric officially debuts on August 21 via the limited-time “Hall Treasures” in-game event. The car can be unlocked using Hall Treasure Coupons to draw from the event pool. Coupons can be acquired through several limited-time mechanics, which can be viewed via the Events menu, within Specials.

Sanjay Shivaram, Brand Licensing & Retail Director at Formula E, said: "China is a key market for Formula E, and teaming up with Porsche to bring the Porsche GEN3 99X Electric to Need for Speed Mobile allows us to connect millions of gamers with the speed of electric performance, and this iconic automotive brand.

"Tencent has brilliantly translated our real-world tech - such as kinetic energy recovery - into the game, and Need for Speed is one of the most famous racing franchises in the world, so we’re thrilled to be able to contribute to its journey.”

title: Reaction from a title-deciding Formula E weekend
excerpt:
The paddock reacts to a title-deciding weekend in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

Pascal Wehrlein

"Under the circumstances we had today, very special. Even though I must say the first one is always a bit more exciting. That's definitely the case, but today it was definitely a tough race. Never expected that what happened would happen, but, anyways, it is what it is. We made it.

"We set the base for today, in the last 15-16 races and we took over the lead yesterday again. The approach of the whole weekend was phenomenal, what a job we've done so far. A bit of an up-and-down season, but again, in the end, you know, when there's pressure on, when it matters, when it counts, we're pretty good.

"Obviously it was a bit unpredictable what Antonio did and how far he took it, but, you know, credits to him for what he did in this race. I think under normal circumstances during that race, we would have had a nice race, probably another podium finish, but nevertheless, I think we achieved what we had to achieve, and we did what we had to do."

Jake Dennis

"There was a clear chance. I think everything we did today, we executed perfectly. We put ourselves in a position to take the title. We were ahead at points, until we weren't. So, yeah, I think we did everything right today.

"I mean, he (Pascal) took me cleanly straight out of the race, so it's as simple as that. I think from my side, it's quite obvious. I think it's embarrassing in what we've seen today from Pascal, Porsche, to be in that position to be Pascal clearly ahead, and then he just rams me straight into the wall. It's quite surprising, but ultimately if they want to win it like that, then they can. But that's the game.

"I can leave London with my head held high. I'm happy with the way I drove, the risks I took, and yeah, I go into the off-season in a pretty good headspace. I have a lot of things personally going on in my life with my fiancée, you know, giving birth in a few weeks, so it's going to be a cool period. GEN4 is going to be exciting, and obviously I'm super busy with BMW still, so from my side an exciting few months coming up, so very much looking forward to it."

Mitch Evans

"I think ultimately we just, unfortunately, both days qualified behind the wrong car. Either a blue and white roadblock for the last two days, and they did all they could to stop me. You know, I managed to get past them in today's race, but ultimately just lost too much ground to the front guys, and yeah, it was for me a little bit extreme, but it is what it is. We did what we had to do on our side to try and give ourselves a shot, and I think we did that. But ultimately we just lost it in quali both days, but we tried and we didn't give up.

"I obviously wanted a different ending to my journey at the team, but wasn't meant to be. I don't leave with many regrets, to be fair. I knew this day was going to come at some point, especially with a lot on the line, and this team's given me so much, and I'm forever grateful for that. They've given me my first professional contract in the sport, and I owe so much to them and everyone that's been involved in the project since day one.

"I'm very proud of what we've achieved, obviously wanted more, we had one last box to check, and we unfortunately haven't done that, but a lot to be proud of. It's going to be weird waking up tomorrow not as a Jaguar driver for the first time. But I just wish them the best for the future."

Ian James (Jaguar TCS Racing)

"I'll be briefly honest, coming into this weekend, I knew how much was at stake in both championships, how much not only Mitch, but we as a team, wanted to deliver the Drivers' Championship for him and for the team as well. And there was always that risk, I suppose, that we'd let our emotions get the better of us. But all credit to the guy on my right (Evans) and to the whole team as well, because the emotions were very much kept in check.

"We approached every session with a clear and level head and executed as well as we possibly could. As Mitch said, qualifying didn't go our way, and that played a huge role then in the outcomes of both races. But at the end of the day, I'm hugely proud of both Mitch and Antonio and the whole team. It's a phenomenal way to deliver a Teams' World Championship."

Thomas Laudenbach (Porsche)

"I have to say that for us, it's great to win again the Manufacturer title. I mean, we are a car manufacturer, but we're also running a team, and but I guess it's the right time to say that this is an effort not only of our team, this is an effort of also the Andretti Formula E team, of CUPRA KIRO, and all together we scored points and secured the title. So for us, that's very important, and we're proud of that. And if you ask me how we celebrate, it's going to be a good one, I can tell you!

"This year the fight with Jaguar, I think that's what the spectators want to see, what the fans want to see. Sometimes the luck is on your side, sometimes you have bad luck. But I mean, that's sport. For today, we are, I think we can all be happy that we provided a good race today for the spectators, and extremely proud of the achievement this season."

title: History in the making: Taylor Barnard becomes Formula E’s youngest winner
excerpt:
On the day that Formula E crowned a new champion, DS PENSKE's Taylor Barnard made some history of his own.

Youngest driver to start a Formula E race, youngest pole sitter and youngest driver to claim a podium. Heading into the final race weekend of the 2025/26 season, DS PENSKE's Taylor Barnard was missing just one record (and arguably the most important one) - to be named Formula E's youngest race winner.

REPORT: Wehrlein navigates dramatic finale to seal Drivers' title as Barnard wins in London

Barnard joined the French squad at the start of the season, following NEOM McLaren's exit from the championship, and despite showing moments of promise and raw pace over the course of the 2025/26 campaign, he has struggled to replicate the impressive points scoring haul of his rookie year.

But heading into the final day of the season, with most eyes on the fight at the head of the championship, British-born Barnard quietly put together a confident and assured performance in qualifying, placing him 6th on the grid for the E-Prix. In the race, Barnard remained in contention throughout, closely following the Mahindra Racing duo of Nyck de Vries and Edoardo Mortara.

The winning moment came in the closing stages of the race, when Barnard's late ATTACK MODE activation saw him able to muscle by Mortara for P2, then polesitter de Vries for the win with a sneaky dive up the inside of the Season 8 champion into the final turn with just two laps left to run.

"I think playing around the championship games was obviously important," said Formula E's newest race winner. "As soon as I got to P3 and I had Antonio behind me, I knew there was going to be some games going on, so it almost felt like a podium secured at that point. And then I was just trying to do everything I can to get as much advantage on the Mahindras as possible.

I didn't think it was going to be possible, they both had two minutes more energy. So, yeah, to be able to get both of them, honestly, is unreal."

At 22 years and 76 days old, Barnard becomes the youngest race winner in Formula E history, taking the record from his DS PENSKE teammate Maximilian Gunther, who won the 2020 Santiago E-Prix at 22 years and 200 days old. And after a long season of highs and lows, surely the result gives the young Brit a big dose of confidence heading into the off season.

"I've now got two complete seasons in Formula E under my belt," he says. "And it's been a long learning process, but obviously the longer I'm going, the more experience I'm getting and the better I'm getting generally at the races, so it's going to keep going. But obviously, it's a massive confidence boost for the team as well. It's been such a tough season, so everybody deserves it."

Taylor Barnard finishes the 2025/26 season 11th in the Drivers' Championship on 68 points.

title: Norman Nato to leave Nissan
excerpt:
Norman Nato and the team have confirmed he'll leave Nissan - and likely Formula E, for now - following the end of the 2025/26 campaign.

The Frenchman exits the team after a two-season spell with the Japanese manufacturer. "I'd like to say a big thank you to everyone at Nissan Formula E Team," he said.

"I've had three great years with the team and we've shared lots of good moments together. Thank you to all the engineers, mechanics and everyone behind the scenes for all the hard work and support. While I now move on to focus on another chapter in my career, I've really enjoyed my time in Formula E, both on the track and around the paddock, and I'm happy to have been part of this championship.

"It's goodbye for now, but I hope to see everyone again soon. I've had three great years with the team and we've shared lots of good moments together. Thank you to all the engineers, mechanics and everyone behind the scenes for all the hard work and support.

"While I now move on to focus on another chapter in my career, I've really enjoyed my time in Formula E, both on the track and around the paddock, and I'm happy to have been part of this championship. It's goodbye for now, but I hope to see everyone again soon."

Nato made his Formula E debut in 2021 with ROKiT Venturi Racing, capping his rookie campaign with a victory in Berlin. Following a reserve role with Jaguar and strong WEC outings, he secured full-time seats with Nissan (Season 9) and Andretti (Season 10), claiming podiums in Rome and Shanghai. Back with Nissan in Season 11, Nato demonstrated front-running pace by taking pole position in Miami.

The 34-year-old scored 20 points in 2025/26 and finished 19th in the Drivers' table.

title: Saudi Arabia wins Formula E’s inaugural 'Best Host Country' award
excerpt:
Presented for the first time in the all-electric championship’s history during the 2025/26 Season Formula E End of Season Awards in London last night, the accolade recognizes the destination that sets the global benchmark for event delivery, infrastructure and partnership.

The Kingdom’s recognition with this prestigious award stands as a testament to its excellence in hosting the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship and to the advanced standards it has established since first hosting the Championship in 2018.

This achievement also reflects the unwavering support extended to the sports sector by the Kingdom’s leadership, under the guidance of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz, Crown Prince and Prime Minister, may Allah protect them. It further reflects the support of His Royal Highness Prince Abdulaziz bin Turki Al Faisal, Minister of Sport; the continued efforts of the Ministry of Sport; and the operational excellence delivered by the Saudi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation, Saudi Motorsport Company, and Sela.

Eng. Mansour Almokbel, Acting CEO of the Saudi Automobile & Motorcycle Federation (SAMF) and CEO of the Saudi Motorsport Company (SMC), said: "We sincerely thank Formula E for this recognition.

"Receiving the Formula E ‘Best Host Country’ award is the result of the collective efforts of everyone who has contributed to hosting and delivering the championship’s races in the Kingdom, from its beginnings in Diriyah through to Jeddah.

"It is a testament to Saudi Arabia’s commitment to staging world-class motorsport events and reflects the strength of our partnerships, expertise and dedication, which continue to elevate the Kingdom’s position on the global motorsport stage.

"Our vision extends far beyond hosting international championships. We are building a sustainable motorsport ecosystem that will inspire future generations, develop Saudi talent and create lasting opportunities across the industry.

"Every event we host is another step towards strengthening Saudi Arabia's position as a global hub for motorsport, and awards such as this reinforce our commitment to continually raising the benchmark for excellence."

Alberto Longo, Co-Founder & Chief Championship Officer of Formula E, said: "The unwavering support and long-term partnership of the Saudi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation, the Saudi Motorsport Company and Ministry of Sport have been instrumental to our journey since 2018.

"Their vital role has helped establish Formula E as a global leader in both motorsport and international events across the Kingdom. Formula E remains deeply aligned to the goals of Vision 2030 and shared vision for a sustainable future.

"We are deeply grateful for their continued commitment, and it is a well-deserved honour to see them recognised with Formula E's inaugural ‘Best Host Country’ award. We look forward to many more years of innovation together."

Saudi Arabia's partnership with Formula E has continued to go from strength to strength since 2018. Following the race’s move from Diriyah to Jeddah in 2025, the inaugural Jeddah E-Prix became the most-watched Formula E race weekend in history, attracting a record 65 million cumulative global viewers.

Jeddah also played a pioneering role in the Championship's continued evolution when it became the first venue to introduce Formula E's innovative PIT BOOST feature in Season 11, with mandatory mid-race pit stops debuting during the Kingdom's double-header before being rolled out across all subsequent double-header events during the season.

Building on a legacy of firsts that has come to define the Kingdom's place in global motorsport, Saudi Arabia will host the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship’s 2026/27 Season opening double-header weekend on December 18–19, 2026 and continue its tradition of delivering landmark moments for Formula E. The event will mark the competitive debut of Formula E's revolutionary GEN4 race car, ushering in a new era for the all-electric championship with faster performance, greater efficiency and enhanced racing.

As Saudi Arabia celebrates this achievement, the Kingdom looks ahead to many more years of partnership with Formula E, delivering world-class racing, pioneering innovation, and unforgettable experiences that continue to elevate the championship on the global stage.

title: Maximilian Günther confirms DS PENSKE exit
excerpt:
The German has announced he'll move on, as DS Automobiles' longstanding spell as a brand in Formula E - most recently alongside the PENSKE operation - drew to a close at the conclusion of the London finale.

Maximilian Günther has announced that he'll be leaving DS PENSKE following the conclusion of the 2025/26 campaign in London this past weekend.

After initially serving as a Reserve Driver, Günther made full-time Formula E debut with Dragon in Season 5. Moving to BMW i Andretti Motorsport for Season 6, he became Formula E's youngest race winner with victories in Santiago and Berlin. Following a brief stint with Nissan e.dams, he joined Maserati MSG Racing for Seasons 9 and 10, claiming multiple podiums and wins in Jakarta and Tokyo.

The German moved to DS PENSKE for GEN3 Evo, and made history by taking the first-ever PIT BOOST victory and leading home a team 1-2 finish in Shanghai after teammate Jean-Eric Vergne's last-lap heroics.

Paddock rumours over the weekend suggest the 29-year-old will likely remain for GEN4, with news of his potential destination to arrive in due course.

DS' decorated Formula E spell comes to a close, for now

DS Automobiles is one of the most decorated manufacturers in Formula E history, famously becoming the first brand to secure back-to-back double titles.

Joining the series in Season 2, the marque secured four titles, 19 victories, and 55 podiums across 151 races.

Taylor Barnard ensured the team signed off in style with a finale victory in London.

The Brit became the youngest-ever race winner in Formula E history at 22 years and 76 days with his penultimate lap move on Nyck de Vries (Mahindra) for the win in Round 17.

Stellantis will be represented in the Manufacturers' stakes by the Opel and Citroen brands from 2026/27 as the GEN4 gets underway.

title: Pascal Wehrlein wins his second Formula E Drivers' World Championship
excerpt:
Pascal Wehrlein survived a dramatic season finale in London to secure his second Formula E World Championship.

Porsche's Pascal Wehrlein clinched his second Formula E Drivers' World Championship after surviving a tense season finale at the London Excel.. The German driver joins Jean-Eric Vergne (Citroën Racing) as the only two-time series champions in the history of the all-electric championship..

Wehrlein came into the double-header weekend third in the standings behind Jake Dennis (Andretti) and Mitch Evans (Jaguar TCS Racing), but after securing the Julius Baer Pole Position and victory on Saturday he was able to finish the race without scoring any points to take the crown.

"I mean the emotions have cooled down a bit," Wehrlein said after being crowned champion. "The happiness is increasing more and more. What we did in this season was again outstanding. I think we could have made our life a bit easier and have decided that championship already earlier, but I guess it would be boring if it was decided earlier as well!

"Today was intense. A lot of games being played, far beyond the line, but it is what it is. Still kept our head cool and brought it home. So, yeah, a special thanks to my team to everyone involved in that project, we are the most successful manufacturer in this GEN3 era and I couldn't be happier and more proud of the team. This one is for them.

"You know, I give everything for them. I put my heart out there and I know it's the same the other way. They give everything for me and yeah, it's been such a great journey together."

Supported by his Porsche teammate Nico Müller, Wehrlein controlled the indoor-outdoor track to capture maximum points on Saturday, building a five-point championship lead over Dennis heading into Sunday.

However, he found himself embroiled in a battle with Jaguar’s António Félix da Costa, who engaged in aggressive defensive tactics to assist teammate Mitch Evans' title push. Both Wehrlein and other title rival Jake Dennis also clashed on-track, but it was Wehrlein who finished ahead and ended the year on 169 points to Dennis' 164.

title: Jaguar TCS Racing take home the 2025/26 Teams' World Championship
excerpt:
It all came down to the final day of the season in both the Drivers' and Teams' championships, with Antonio Felix da Costa and Mitch Evans playing the team game to perfection to give Jaguar TCS Racing their second Formula E Teams' title.

REPORT: Wehrlein navigates dramatic finale to seal Drivers' title as Barnard wins in London

Heading into race day, the British-based squad led the way in the standings, with Porsche needing to outscore their rivals in order to clinch the silverware - having already beaten Jaguar in the hunt for the Manufacturers' World Championship in Tokyo.

In a frantic title-deciding race, both teams experienced dramatic highs and lows with da Costa doing his bit via an impressive defensive performance, holding off a charging Pascal Wehrlein for a large portion of the E-Prix. The Portuguese driver eventually crossed the chequered flag in 15th, but his relentless defensive strategy helped his teammate pick up the critical championship points.

"Antonio, from the minute he got into the team, has been just incredibly collaborative," said Jaguar TCS Racing Team Principal Ian James. "What we saw from him today was, again, a strategy that was executed perfectly, some really, really good driving, some really hard but fair driving, and that's helped to deliver the championship as well.

"As we know, over the past few races, they haven't always gone our way. I don't know if I should believe in the racing gods. I'm very much a somebody that says that you make your own luck, but if I look back over this season, we've definitely been on the wrong side of the lucky penny from time to time. But I think at the end of the day, that doesn't take anything away from what both drivers have achieved, and we as a team will be eternally grateful for that."

For Evans, it was a bittersweet day, in his last race for Jaguar, he finished the day in 4th - having qualified in 5th - which was not enough for him to clinch his first Formula E Drivers' Championship, but did enable Jaguar to extend their lead in the standings to a comfortable 17 points.

"Obviously I knew this day was going to come at some point," said the Kiwi. "This team's given me so much, and I'm forever grateful for that. They've given me my first professional contract in the sport, and I owe so much to them and everyone that's been involved in the project since day one.

"I'm very proud of what we've achieved. Obviously wanted more, we had one last box to check, and we unfortunately haven't done that, but a lot to be proud of, and yeah, it's going to be weird waking up tomorrow not as a Jaguar driver for the first time. But, you know, I just wish them the best for the future, and yeah, on my side, exciting times ahead for my next adventure."
